deep.reconstruction:
Context (from the previous and next pages): in October 1819 Gauss is examining the graduation (division) errors of the divided circle of the Göttingen meridian circle. He uses several reading microscopes and a test microscope ('Prüfungsmikroskop', set to 0 on 15 Oct.). On Oct. 16 he defined the scheme I = z + c', II = z + 270° + c'', III = z + 90° + c''', O = z + 45°. Here z is the nominal division under the reference microscope, and c', c'', c''' are the measured deviations in arc-seconds, taken every 15° over the full circle (24 settings).

This page, headed 'Oct. 17, wie gestern' ('as yesterday'), repeats the same observing scheme the next day.

(1) The table has 24 rows z = 0, 15, ..., 345°. Each row gives three numbers, c'(z), c''(z) and c'''(z) in seconds, for microscopes I, II and III. Above the third column stands an underlined '-0.4'. My interpretation: this is a constant reduction still to be applied to the c''' column. The column sums are 0.65, 0.80 and 8.35, so the means are about +0.03, +0.03 and +0.35. Subtracting 0.4 brings the third mean to about -0.05, i.e. to the same near-zero level as the other two. This matches the closure condition that division errors sum to zero round the whole circle, with the constant absorbed into the microscope offset.

(2) The small box gives II - I = +1'47.7" and III - I = -1'28.4". These are the mean angular separations of microscopes II and III from I, beyond their nominal 270° and 90°. They agree with the previous day's values (+1'48.7", -1'28.3") to about 1" and 0.1".

(3) Purpose, from the surrounding pages (my inference): as on Oct. 16, sums of the c columns at suitably shifted arguments are to be represented by a finite trigonometric series a0 + sum_{k=1..12} (a_k cos kz + b_k sin kz). The 24 equidistant points determine harmonics up to k = 12. Combinations of microscope positions are chosen so that certain harmonics cancel; the next page shows a series containing only even cosine terms.

(4) The column at the right edge belongs to the facing (next) page. It is the scheme I z, II z+270, III z+90, O z+315 together with column I of that table. It is not part of the Oct. 17 work.

No derivation is carried out on this page itself: it is raw observational data plus the microscope separations.
errors: No computational errors detectable; the page is a raw data record.
Column III has mean about +0.35" rather than about 0, hence the marginal -0.4 reduction (interpretation, not certain).

results.what: Systematic measurement of circle-graduation errors at 15° intervals with several microscopes at fixed angular offsets, prepared for representation by a finite Fourier series (24 points, harmonics up to 12)
results.modern_name: Calibration of divided circles / harmonic analysis of graduation errors (trigonometric interpolation, discrete Fourier analysis)
results.usually_credited_to: Graduation-error investigations: Bessel (Königsberg, 1819-1830s), later Hansen and others; trigonometric interpolation at equidistant points: Gauss (Theoria interpolationis, c. 1805), Clairaut and Lagrange earlier

results.what: Determination of the microscope separations II-I and III-I as mean offsets

deep.surprise_reason: Raw calibration data for the Göttingen meridian circle. Gauss's trigonometric interpolation and his instrumental work around 1819-20 are known, and similar error analysis was being done by Bessel at the time. Nothing non-standard appears on this page.

checkable.asserts: Sum of column c' = 0.65 (mean about 0.03, i.e. near zero)
Mean of column c''' is about 0.348, consistent with the marginal -0.4 reduction
II-I changed by -1.0" from Oct. 16 to Oct. 17

transcription_corrections: The underlined '-0.4' stands specifically above the third (c''') column, not as a general heading.
The right-edge header reads 'I z', 'II z+270', 'III z+90', 'O z+315' (the '2' is the letter z); this column belongs to the facing page, not to Oct. 17.
Right-edge values 30: -6.3, 105: -5.3, 120: -5.3 are confirmed by the next-page transcription.
